text:
anya: :rotating_light: Seeing a p99 jump on hosted-api from ~280ms -> ~1.4s starting ~11:03 UTC. p95 also up. Queues spiking on runtime pools.
ben: Noted. Any tenant spikes or is this cross-tenant?
anya: Mostly cross-tenant but one big tenant shows sustained Q depth on host pool-7. KV cache miss rate up ~3x for that host group.
cheng: Can you paste the metric ranges? cpu/mem/gpu util and queue_depth?
anya: metrics snippet:
```
host=pool-7 queue_depth: 26 -> 140
p95: 290ms -> 960ms
p99: 420ms -> 1.43s
kvcache_miss_rate: 4% -> 12%
kernel_switch_count(slow): 18 -> 210
```
ben: kernel_switch_count(slow) rising suggests kernel selector falling back to non-quantized kernels. Any recent rollout to kernel heuristics?
dalia: I rolled a heuristic tweak to prefer 'safe' kernels for 2s longer sequences yesterday evening (rev rtx-heur-2026-03). Could be related.
anya: timeline matches. Also see continuous_batching average batch size jump -> more KV cache flushes and stale KV shards.
eng-oncall: tagging oncall. @eng-oncall can you check host-level IO and swap? Could be noisy neighbor or OOM-driven evictions.
eng-oncall: Looking now — disk IOPS normal, no swap. But one VM on pool-7 shows high process context switches and GPU SM stalls. PID 18432 is running a heavy sampling job from tenant-A.
ben: Tenant-A doing long-samples could blow KV cache if we have prefix diversity. Can we throttle or isolate tenant-A to a dedicated queue?
anya: Short mitigation proposal:
- revert rtx-heur-2026-03 for kernel selector on pool-7 (rollback to previous model)
- temporarily pin tenant-A to limited concurrency
- force KV prefetch expiry for pool-7 to clear bad entries
- enable fallback to smaller batch sizes for pool-7
Any objections?
cheng: +1 to rollback and smaller batches. Prefetch expiry might be disruptive but ok as short-term.
dalia: I'll prepare rollback PR and a canary patch to only affect pool-7. Deploy-bot can run staged rollout.
deploy-bot: Deploy request received: revert/rtx-heur-2026-03 -> target: pool-7 canary 10%. Command: `ci deploy --tag revert-rtx-heur-2026-03 --targets pool-7 --canary 10`.
anya: While deploy goes, can we get a flamegraph / perf profile from the slow PID? `perf record -F 99 -p 18432 -- sleep 30` and `perf script | flamegraph.pl > flame.svg`
eng-oncall: Collected perf — attaching top hotspots: kernel_selector.cpp:select(), continuous_batcher::dispatch(), kvcache::evict_if_needed(). GPU kernels show longer launch latency due to context switching.
ben: That aligns — kernel_selector is doing extra checks and falling back to slower code path under higher sequence variance. The change likely increased selector cost and made it prefer conservative kernels when miss rate > X.
anya: After canary rollback at 10% we see immediate p95 drop on those hosts: p95 -> 320ms, p99 -> 520ms. kvcache_miss_rate back to ~4.5% in canary nodes.
dalia: Rolling to 100% on pool-7 now.
deploy-bot: Rollout 10% -> 100% completed for target pool-7. Status: success.
anya: Post-rollout metrics on pool-7: queue_depth down to 20-30 range, p95 ~310-350ms, p99 ~480-600ms. Kernel_switch_count(slow) back to baseline.
cheng: Root cause summary draft: recent kernel-selector heuristic (rtx-heur-2026-03) increased conservative kernel selection for sequences crossing threshold, causing more slower kernel fallbacks and larger batch sizes. This increased KV cache churn (higher miss rate) and queue depth. Combined with a heavy long-sample workload from Tenant-A, host pool-7 saw amplified effects.
ben: Action items:
- revert heuristic (done)
- add metric alert for kernel_selector.fallback_rate > 5% in 2m window
- add per-tenant long-sample throttling guard for hosted-api
- add unit test / perf regression test that simulates sequence-length variance
- update rollout checklist to canary heuristic changes on a small set before global
anya: I'll file the follow-ups and assign owners. Also recommend a small change: fallback cost model should consider kvcache_miss_rate before preferring safe kernels.
dalia: assigning: ben -> alert, cheng -> perf tests, anya -> tenant throttling PR, dalia -> selector cost model PR.
eng-oncall: closing loop: p95/p99 stabilized, keeping monitoring for next 24h. If anything flares, paging rules are enabled.
anya: Thanks all. Good catch on the Tenant-A noisy sampling. :thumbsup:
